method: Configuration-level reassessment: the plan's mitigations are applied to a deep copy of the original request exactly as Simulation.mitigate changes a device (TLS configuration update, device re-authentication, certificate issuance, log scrubbing, prompt redaction or filtering); the same agent pipeline is then re-run with the same seed. The projected score assumes each selected action removes only its own finding. Plan A: shipped planner (independent per-finding actions). Plan B: shared-root-cause planner (actions whose remediation is the same mitigation merged into one decision unit costed once: max cost / downtime / complexity of the members, summed benefit). Exhaustive check: for scenarios with at most 10 candidate actions, every subset of per-finding actions feasible under the independent accounting and every subset of whole root-cause groups feasible under the grouped accounting is reassessed with one full pipeline run; outcomes are ranked by (PQ score, environment status, remaining findings) and the cheapest subset attaining the best outcome is reported per accounting. Plan A is compared with the independent enumeration, plan B with the grouped one. 'Summed benefit' is the sum of the selected actions' optimization_benefit; 'projected' is the explainer's plan_projection, which assumes each action removes only its own finding.
caveat: Network mitigations (rate limiting, segmentation) cannot be modelled at configuration level because the model cannot observe post-mitigation traffic: iot_traffic is left unchanged and traffic findings remain. Record-level PHI remediation of ehr_records is not modelled. Scenarios are synthetic.
